mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate relative to historical averages compresses discount rates for equity valuation, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in >60% of periods with FEDFUNDS below 4.0% (10th percentile), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 5.0% signals an aggressive monetary tightening cycle, which increases the cost of capital and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in >60% of periods with FEDFUNDS > 5.0, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate and acceleration in payroll employment growth signals a tightening labor market that typically precedes monetary policy tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls > 0.2pp and PAYEMS growth > 0.5% MoM
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in >60% of instances with UNRATE fall >0.2pp and PAYEMS growth >0.5% MoM, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, strong housing starts and retail sales growth signal overheating demand, which typically triggers monetary policy tightening and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in >60% of instances with HOUST >1800.0 and RSAFS >365000.0 during late-cycle expansion, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production growth signals strong economic output, which supports corporate earnings growth and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in >60% of periods with INDPRO growth >0.5% MoM, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the CPI index above 205 signals persistent inflation, which typically prompts the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in >60% of periods with CPIAUCSL > 205, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, a low unemployment rate (below 4.0%) and strong payroll employment growth (above 0.5% MoM) signal an overheating labor market that typically triggers wage inflation and subsequent monetary tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in >60% of instances with UNRATE <4.0 and PAYEMS growth >0.5% MoM during late-cycle expansion, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate above 5.0% and CPI index above 205 signals an aggressive monetary tightening cycle in response to persistent inflation, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in >60% of instances with FEDFUNDS >5.0 and CPIAUCSL >205, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
